My wife was hospitalized here after a spinal-operation. After just 5 days, in great pain and unable to move, she phoned my crying and begging to please bring her home.

When arriving at the hospital I found her alone dumped on a metal-bed outside the hospital entrance. Nowhere physically ready to go home, but she was desperate to get away from what she described as “Hell on earth”.

Nurses deliberately ignoring patients asking for help and their cry’s for pain killers, talking bad to patients, treating them like “pieces of meat” and ignoring doctors orders like e.g. turning her every 2 hours. The list goes on… She even experienced being picked up by a drunk porter, who caused her extreme pain, by the rough way he handled transporting her to x-ray. When she noticed the other staff of it, she was just ignored and talked bad to.

My wife has had cancer for 6 years, experienced a lot of hospitals in Thailand. She is not the type to complain or whine. But this is not a place she would wish for even her worst enemy to end up at.

The good: There was ONE nurse on the ward (a ladyboy) who treated the patients extremely well. She was the only light of the day and should have all the praise she deserves.

Government hospital, over-worked or not… Management and the bad behaving staff at this hospital, should be extremely embarrassed of the way they treat and disrespect their fellow human beings. At least show some compassion, empathy for others and respect for your work.

Inefficient, bogged down with endless paper work. Often have to go several times for an appointment because of lack of doctors and poor scheduling of appointments. They place priority on forms rather than the well-being of the patient.

Have reduced this from 2 stars to 1 star after they nearly killed my mother-in-law due to total lack of patient care and mismanagement in her treatment. Had to rush her to ICU in another hospital after 2 months or so of treatment at Nakornping Hospital. She was in the other hospital for 6 days. She is  out now, can speak and walk now. A big change from when she was at NP Hospital. She couldn't walk, could barely breathe and had a blood pressure of over 200 which didn't seem to bother them in the slightest as they sent her out the door. I think they didn't want to treat her as an inpatient in case she died whilst in their questionable care.

Had to come for pre-arranged appointment to see the neurologist. We went in with dog bites me and my girlfriend got while riding my bicycle. The ER doctor prescribed a treatment, thetanus shot, rabies shot, antibiotics, hemoglobulin. Then sent me to the cashier and it turned out to be 3000 THB each. I thought it was preposterous, but above all we didn't have that kind of money on us. They were going to send us away without treatment which I very much think it's a violation of the Hipocratic Oath. After actually yelling at the doctor, which is not a thing they're used to in Thailand for sure, he told us the hemoglobulin is not mandatory and he could just give us the shots and the antibiotics. It finally went down to 1300 THB for the both of us.

The installations themselves looked pretty good. The toilet was filthy

They always answer patients' questions, even if they ask the same questions multiple times. Even elderly patients whose relatives haven't arrived yet are well cared for, and they chat and joke with them. It's such lovely behavior. I've seen the doctors, nurses, and assistants provide excellent care. They are very kind and don't get emotional with patients. Their care, including feeding, is outstanding; they pay attention to patients, and remind them to eat and take their medicine. I'm very impressed. I've discreetly asked other patients and their relatives, and almost everyone agrees that it's excellent. I'd also like to thank the physical therapy team. They are kind and caring. During physical therapy sessions, they greet patients warmly and are very attentive. Physical therapy is never boring because everyone helps each other so well. Finally, I want to thank the doctors, nurses, assistants, and the entire physical therapy team for their dedication and hard work. Thank you so much. Regardless of the patient's condition, they need the best possible care. 🙏🏻🙏🏻

I would like to propose expanding or increasing the number of service points for the home delivery of medicine, sir. The current service is insufficient to accommodate the large number of patients, resulting in very long waiting times, despite the hospital having improved its services. Please consider this proposal, sir.

Okay, let me explain. I arrived at 5:30 PM and waited because I had abdominal pain. When I informed them, it turned out I only had to wait for a blood test. I sat outside for 3.5 hours, then waited another 30 minutes inside the room. The problem is, my lab results took almost 3 hours. Then, after the results came out, I waited another 1.5 hours. During this time, I asked about twice if it was my turn, and they just kept saying "wait a minute" and then said something else I couldn't understand. I walked outside and vented my anger by kicking the ground. It was the first time I'd ever experienced this. I waited for over 9 hours, almost 10 hours. People who came after me had already finished and gone home. I sat there until I felt like I was going to grow roots. It's 2:00 AM now, and I still don't know if I have appendicitis or enteritis. Waiting 4-5 hours is understandable, but this is 9, almost 10 hours! Everyone who came after me has already left. Who could tolerate that? This is the first time I've ever waited this long. Even someone with similar symptoms who came in after me finished first. I had a fever and my stomach hurt. Sometimes I don't dare ask often because I'm afraid of bothering them, but this time I really can't take it anymore. I waited until I was playing games with friends and my battery was almost dead. That's really too much.

text: Based on my and my family's experience over the past 10 years, the doctors here have never correctly diagnosed a patient's condition. From gallbladder issues mistaken for gastritis, to brain trauma related to the eyes not being detected, to broken arms requiring metal plates not being considered, kidney stones not being found and successfully treated elsewhere, insomnia caused by irregular eating habits not being diagnosed, autism not being diagnosed, and minor abnormalities in children not being detected and referred to developmental institutes instead. Even sleep apnea wasn't initially diagnosed. Therefore, it can be concluded that this place may be suitable for general illnesses, but for complex conditions, my family's 10 years of experience confirms that coming here is a life-threatening risk.

Today, I took my mother to the doctor and observed a patient with low blood pressure. For over 30 minutes, while calling for the stretcher bearer, I saw Nurse Sasikarn Rojchanaratnangkoon continuously measuring the patient's blood pressure and attempting to contact and coordinate with the staff about five times to ensure the patient arrived as quickly as possible. The patient's blood pressure eventually dropped to around 80/40 before the patient was finally picked up.

What impressed me most was her coordination in contacting the stretcher bearer. Her enthusiasm, attention to detail, and unwavering dedication to helping the patient demonstrated the spirit of a nurse who prioritizes patient safety.

I would like to express my sincere gratitude to Nurse Sasikarn Rojchanaratnangkoon for her dedication, sacrifice, and heartfelt service. It was a truly impressive experience.
